title: 5 Best Markdown to HTML Converters in 2026 (Free Tools)
description: Discover the top Markdown to HTML converters for 2026. Free online tools, browser extensions, and CLI options for every workflow.

sections.heading: Why Convert Markdown to HTML?
sections.content: Markdown is the writer's format of choice — clean, readable, and portable. But the web runs on HTML. Whether you're publishing a blog post, sending an email newsletter, or updating a website, you'll need to convert Markdown to HTML. The right tool preserves your formatting, handles code blocks correctly, and saves you from writing raw HTML tags.

sections.heading: 1. MarkdownMagic — Best Free Online Converter
sections.content:
MarkdownMagic offers the cleanest conversion experience with zero friction. No account needed, instant preview, and bidirectional conversion (HTML back to Markdown). It handles GitHub-flavored Markdown including tables, task lists, and code blocks with syntax highlighting. The live preview lets you catch formatting issues before exporting.

Pros: Free, no signup, live preview, bidirectional, GFM support
Cons: Online only

sections.heading: 2. Dillinger — Full-Featured Online Editor
sections.content:
Dillinger is a cloud-enabled Markdown editor with export options. Write in Markdown on the left, see HTML preview on the right. Export to HTML, PDF, or styled Markdown. Integration with Dropbox, Google Drive, and GitHub makes it a complete writing environment.

Pros: Cloud sync, multiple export formats, integrations
Cons: Requires account for cloud features

sections.heading: 3. Marked 2 — Best for macOS Users
sections.content:
Marked 2 is a premium Markdown previewer for Mac that exports clean HTML. It watches your files and updates the preview in real-time. The export includes customizable CSS themes and handles advanced Markdown features. At $13.99, it's affordable for professionals who write regularly.

Pros: Real-time preview, beautiful themes, file watching
Cons: macOS only, paid software

sections.heading: 4. Pandoc — The Swiss Army Knife
sections.content:
Pandoc converts between virtually every document format. Markdown to HTML is just one of hundreds of transformations it handles. Command-line interface means it's scriptable and integrates into build pipelines. The learning curve is steep, but power users swear by it.

Pros: Handles any format, scriptable, free and open source
Cons: Command line only, complex options

sections.heading: 5. Typora — Best WYSIWYG Experience
sections.content:
Typora eliminates the split view — you edit Markdown directly and formatting appears as you type. Export to HTML, PDF, Word, and more. It's the closest thing to a traditional word processor for Markdown users. Recently moved to a paid model ($14.99) but worth it for heavy writers.

Pros: Seamless editing experience, multiple exports
Cons: Now paid software, no live source view

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Markdown Converter
sections.content:
For occasional conversions, MarkdownMagic is unbeatable — free, fast, and no account required. Writers who need a full environment should try Dillinger. Mac users who write daily should consider Marked 2 or Typora. Developers and automation enthusiasts need Pandoc in their toolkit.

Consider your workflow: Do you need live preview? Cloud sync? Command-line access? The best tool is the one that fits how you work, not the one with the most features.
